subject: eraevous/MtG
decision: Import the 2026-10-25 handoff code as-is (kb/, grammar/, review_packet/, evaluations/, predictions/) into the AEC-template repo, replace the template docs with MTG ones, and add a minimal AEC layer (project purpose, purpose files, drift_check, ledgers, CI). Restructuring comes later.
reason: One build rather than parallel builds. Reuse the existing implementation. Kate: 'The repository is infrastructure for the Magic project. The Magic project is not an excuse to build infrastructure.'

subject: codex_++/project.purpose.md
decision: Adopt P-00 (project purpose) plus P-01 to P-05, with P-01 amended so that unverified grammar and KB output stays a candidate, and authority scoped by subject rather than one linear ranking.
reason: Kate's review of the first draft: the original P-01 gave unreviewed automation too much authority, and the linear hierarchy let inventory appear to outrank Oracle.

subject: VISION.md, CHARTER.md (MTG product charter)
decision: Add two commitments to the MTG charter: conversational interoperability (the analysis is exposed as read-only tools that outside conversational AIs can call, CLI/JSON before MCP) and open-ended exploration (exploration works without an existing deck, and supports both LLM-directed and system-surfaced discovery). Consider splitting the phases into Conceive -> Explore -> Evaluate -> Decide.
reason: Zach wants a system he and others (e.g. Steph planning a Terra deck) can ask exploratory questions of, with an LLM in the loop. Kate and the build Claude agreed on a six-verb read-only tool surface.

subject: mtgtools check, links, collection policy
decision: (1) check separates evidence_grade (how good the source is) from verdict (SUPPORTED / CONTRADICTED / UNKNOWN / NOT_CHECKED for a structured assertion); grade is decision_grade only when a decision-grade source settles the assertion. Free text is never judged. (2) Links carry a qualifier status (compatible / unresolved / incompatible) from recorded qualifiers; incompatible links are rejected and reported, unknown qualifiers stay unresolved; same-card and self-enter (copy or return of a target) links are admitted with that status. (3) Loops the KB contradicts are listed as contested and never hide a card's other interactions. (4) decks/collection_policy.json records who may use the collection and which decks are protected; context and card report it. Not applied to the frozen Terra runs 1-2.
reason: Terra runs 1-2 (2026-10-27): check graded a false availability claim decision_grade; energy/lore and artifact-type false links; Banishing Light false negative; Decoction Module discarded wholesale in run 2.
evidence: terra-v0 run1/run2 transcripts and Kate's assessments (relay files on Zach's PC, 2026-10-27); tests/test_mtgtools.py regressions

subject: inventory input (collection/, kb/vendor/mtg_eval/collection_db.py)
decision: Add a bring-your-own collection database (SQLite, collection/schema.sql) as a second inventory input beside the canonical Sheet export. The evaluator and the v0.1 KB build accept either file at the same argument; the reader returns the Sheet's Collection and Deck Allocations rows so nothing downstream changes. Imports cover collection-app CSVs, a Sheet .xlsx (canonical layout or one tab) and text decklists; card data comes from Scryfall. For Zach the Sheet stays the inventory authority and the release pipeline stays on the .xlsx export.
reason: Zach (2026-10-27): the repo is public but the Sheet is restricted, so others cannot run anything; he wants others to bring their own Sheet or (preferably) SQLite database, with setup docs, falling back to Zach-only if that gets onerous. It did not: the adapter already had one seam (raw tab rows), so the change touches two pinned kb files.
evidence: Zach's 2026-10-24d export imported into a collection DB gives identical adapter health, facts, deck lists and operations, and a byte-identical Token Triumph evaluator report

subject: codex_++/project.purpose.md P-05
decision: Proposed P-05 wording: 'Actual ownership and deck allocation, read from the user's canonical inventory (for Zach, the inventory Sheet; for anyone else, their collection database), are authoritative inputs for any recommendation that user can act on.' The rest of P-05 and fixture F-P05 are unchanged. Not applied: the purpose file changes only with Zach's approval.
reason: P-05 currently names only the Sheet. With D-0003 the same contract has to hold for a collection database; its intent (respect the real collection, plans are not moves, label unowned cards) is unchanged.

subject: kb/kbq.py overlap(); mtgtools context --deck roles
decision: Deck role summaries report detected role candidates: `sole_detected_candidates` ({role: {card, evidence}}) and `reviewed_role_counts`, replacing `single_source_roles`; mtgtools context adds an exploratory caveat claim that a sole detected candidate is not a verified sole provider. The KB wipe detector excludes flicker, own-side and helper/blocker-only scopes (kb patch 3, release r20261028).
reason: Both arms of the 2026-10-28 paired run treated a regex false positive (Golden Argosy as sole wipe) as a protected singleton. Kate's audit recommended a narrow classifier fix plus clearer evidence status.

subject: kb patch 4: roles from predefined tokens and token-making keywords
decision: Role detection reads predefined token names (Treasure, Gold: ramp+fixing; Lander: ramp+fixing+land_drop; Powerstone: ramp; Clue: draw; Food: lifegain_source) when the card creates them, and token-making keywords (incubate, afterlife, living weapon, for mirrodin!, mobilize, offspring, fabricate, squad, embalm, eternalize, myriad: token_maker; extort: closer). Reminder text stays stripped. Junk, Blood and Map carry no role.
reason: Role audit v0.2: two of three confirmed untagged misses were reminder-text tokens. Zach OK'd the mapping work 2026-10-29 02:52Z.

subject: strategic role definitions for deck summaries (kb capability roles, kbq.overlap, mtgtools context)
decision: (1) One-shot sacrifice (ETB or spell) is not a sac_outlet; record it as a qualifier and as a generator of sacrifice triggers, if that role exists. (2) Flashback and other self-reuse are not recursion; record them as self_reuse. (3) Token multipliers (Queen Allenal type) make tokens only together with another token maker: classify them as a composite role if one is available, otherwise as token_multiplier. (4) Cards that create Treasure, Food or Clue tokens are token makers; the tokens themselves count under ramp, lifegain or draw as relevant. (5) Fixing is reported as two numbers: mana-base colour access (lands) and nonland fixing. (6) A one-time drain of 2 is not a closer.
reason: Role-detector audit v0.1 and Kate's spot-check showed that many hits and misses depend on what a role means. Kate recommended settling definitions before measuring recall or changing detectors.
evidence: Zach's reply in the build thread, 2026-10-28T22:39:27Z

subject: strategic role definitions: primary meanings not covered by D-0008
decision: Primary meanings per the role-definitions doc table. spot_removal: removes or neutralises one opposing permanent; conditional weakening is a qualifier. protection: protects other permanents you control; self-only is a qualifier. recursion: returns or recasts other cards from your graveyard. ramp: repeatable mana beyond the land drop; rituals and restricted or conditional mana are qualifiers. draw: draws for net card advantage; loot, cycling, wheels and symmetric draw are qualifiers. sac_outlet: repeatable at-will sacrifice of another permanent. token_maker: creates tokens itself. closer: a credible route to ending the game (repeatable drain or damage, scaling team pump or evasion, alternate win). wipe: removes most creatures or permanents.
reason: Zach answered the six flagged questions (D-0008) but did not explicitly accept the rest of the table, so it stays proposed.

subject: strategic role definitions: D-0009 with Kate's operational clarifications
decision: As D-0009, except: ramp = increases mana production or speeds up mana development beyond normal land drops, so one-shot land ramp counts, with qualifiers persistent / repeatable / ritual / restricted / conditional. fixing = YES only when the card improves colour flexibility (makes or finds more than one colour); lands record their producible colours. draw = net card advantage, naming any resource spent; cycling and other self-replacing draws (replacement) and loot are not draw. Answer scale: YES includes ordinary costs and game-state requirements; DEPENDS only for a nontrivial outside enabler, an unusually restrictive setup or a disputed reading.
reason: Kate's review of the v0.2 packets: the earlier ramp wording excluded Rampant Growth, and fixing, draw and DEPENDS were not operational enough for agreement testing.

subject: copy effects and impulse draw in role classification
decision: (1) A generic copy effect does not fill the role of whatever it might copy: answer NO with qualifier copy_effect. The system must handle copy ontologically (a copy takes on the copied object's behavior), not the role table. Exception: when the copy ability is specific, e.g. 'copy a creature token you control', classify by what it can copy. (2) Impulse draw (exile and you may play it) is NOT draw: answer NO with qualifier impulse. Exile-and-play does not trigger 'whenever you draw' effects, so counting it as draw would misalign triggers and listeners. Zach is open to counterarguments for purposes other than draw triggers.
reason: Zach, 2026-10-29 02:49Z, answering the two policy questions in role audit v0.2.

subject: temporary neutralisation is not spot_removal
decision: Effects that only tap a permanent, stun it, or stop it attacking or blocking for a turn or so are tempo control, not spot_removal (qualifier temporary_neutralisation). spot_removal's 'neutralise' means a lasting effect, such as an aura or a static ability that keeps the permanent from acting.
reason: Kate 2026-10-29: the guide says 'removes or neutralises', which leaves room for Homesickness-style effects. Audit v0.2 adjudicated NO; the rule makes that reproducible.

subject: temporary neutralisation is not spot_removal
decision: As D-0013: effects that only tap, stun, or stop a permanent attacking or blocking for a turn or so are tempo control, not spot_removal (qualifier temporary_neutralisation). spot_removal's 'neutralise' means a lasting effect, such as an aura or a static ability that keeps the permanent from acting.
reason: Zach accepted the rule from PR #13 on 2026-10-30 ('I accept that rule in PR 13, yes').

subject: agents ground card and interaction answers in the KB and DIO, and say when they cannot
decision: (1) Before any card, deck or interaction analysis an agent runs tools/kb_bootstrap.py status, installs the pinned KB release if it is missing, and follows docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md (mtgtools card/explore/hypothesis, DIO sections via mtgtools dio). (2) Every such answer ends with a grounding line: KB release and level, DIO sections relied on, which cards were agent-annotated, and 'not KB-grounded' when the KB was unavailable. (3) The KB release zip is distributed as a GitHub release asset named in tools/kb_release.json and verified against kb/MANIFEST.sha256.
reason: Zach's blind Codex test, 2026-10-30: the agent never opened the DIO and had no KB, and nothing told it to.

subject: route construction requests by kind; typal-first path; document precedence; progressive requirements
proposed_by: claude-build (from Zach's blind ChatGPT Merfolk test findings register)
decision: (1) docs/DOCUMENT_PRECEDENCE.md is the maintained source-precedence rule. DIO v3.1.1 with its addendum and A1-A7 governs representation, and Protocol references to DIO v2.x are read as v3.1.1. The inventory is resolved by its exact title, rejecting _ARCHIVE; stored ids are hints. (2) A construction request is routed by what it names: a commander (v1.0), a mechanical thesis (v1.1 inventory-first), a creature type (typal-first: type population, generic type support, clusters, color topology, commander candidates, functional completion), or swaps (v1.2). (3) Requirements are gathered progressively: stated provisional defaults, automatic investigation first, then at most two questions that change the next decision.
reason: The 2026-10-31 blind test: the instructions named an archived inventory id, the procedure had no path for a creature-type request, word search missed the type's support, and older addenda left the governing DIO version ambiguous.

subject: deck decommission is its own portfolio operation
proposed_by: claude-build (from Zach's blind ChatGPT decommission test findings)
decision: Retiring a deck to feed another is routed as DECOMMISSION -> RELEASE AUDIT -> TARGET ABSORPTION (docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md 6.5), not as v1.2 transfers: the donor's engine, replacements and deck floor stop being constraints; physical custody, protected-deck agreement and receiver cuts stay. The release audit credits the decommission only for cards with no free copy elsewhere. Absorption judges intrinsic, extracted and absorbed value separately. Proposed as a v1.2 addendum, not an ontology change.
reason: The 2026-10-31 test found v1.2 has transfer, swap and floor machinery but no route for a retiring donor, and that 10 of Blight Curse's 82 nonbasic names already had free copies.
